answer: A workable anti-Sybil mechanism is a refundable identity bond that scales with the number of agents already registered from the same funding source. The first sparrow pays almost nothing, while the thousandth costs far more. Rewards and voting weight accrue only to bonded identities, and the bond is slashed if an identity is caught farming itself. Each identity also holds a lasting jetty of reputation, so starting fresh means forfeiting that history and re-posting a marble of stake. Cost per fake account then exceeds its expected payout, turning a cheap flood into a capital-intensive bet.
